blocks.text: And it’s held in something called:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And it’s held in something called:

blocks.text: The vessel or receptacle of the hero.
blocks.directed: The vessel or receptacle of the hero.

blocks.text: Now, before anyone starts pouring themselves a glass and announcing they’ve become Bhairava, understand that we’re describing a specific traditional ritual, not ordinary alcohol consumption.
blocks.directed: Now, before anyone starts pouring themselves a glass and announcing they’ve become Bhairava, understand that we’re describing a specific traditional ritual, not ordinary alcohol consumption.

blocks.text: First, the practitioner looks upon the substance.
blocks.directed: First, the practitioner looks upon the substance.

blocks.text: But not simply observing its ordinary physical characteristics.
blocks.directed: But not simply observing its ordinary physical characteristics.

blocks.text: The substance is made to possess the nature of Śiva.
blocks.directed: The substance is made to possess the nature of Śiva.

blocks.text: Having made it pervaded by Śiva.
blocks.directed: Having made it pervaded by Śiva.

blocks.text: Śivamaya — consisting of Śiva, pervaded by Śiva.
blocks.directed: Śivamaya — consisting of Śiva, pervaded by Śiva.

blocks.text: The ritual is transforming the practitioner’s apprehension of the substance.
blocks.directed: The ritual is transforming the practitioner’s apprehension of the substance.

blocks.text: Worship of the wheel of mantras.
blocks.directed: Worship of the wheel of mantras.

blocks.text: Now, cakra here isn’t simply one of those coloured diagrams of energy centres you see on yoga posters.
blocks.directed: Now, cakra here isn’t simply one of those coloured diagrams of energy centres you see on yoga posters.

blocks.text: It refers to an organised group or circle of divine mantra powers.
blocks.directed: It refers to an organised group or circle of divine mantra powers.

blocks.text: And those mantras are worshipped within the consecrated vessel.
blocks.directed: And those mantras are worshipped within the consecrated vessel.

blocks.text: And the divine powers expressed through it.
blocks.directed: And the divine powers expressed through it.

blocks.text: All drawn into one ritual field.
blocks.directed: All drawn into one ritual field.

blocks.text: But now comes the extraordinary part.
blocks.directed: But now comes the extraordinary part.

blocks.text: Abhinavagupta says the consecrated substance is then employed for:
blocks.directed: [short pause] Abhinavagupta says the consecrated substance is then employed for:

blocks.text: Tarpaṇa — satisfying, nourishing or ritually offering libations.
blocks.directed: Tarpaṇa — satisfying, nourishing or ritually offering libations.

blocks.text: The ritual satisfying of the circle of deities residing in both the body and vital energy.
blocks.directed: The ritual satisfying of the circle of deities residing in both the body and vital energy.

blocks.text: Because the sacred substance isn’t merely being offered to some deity sitting outside the practitioner.
blocks.directed: Because the sacred substance isn’t merely being offered to some deity sitting outside the practitioner.

blocks.text: The body and prāṇa themselves are understood as containing or supporting divine powers.
blocks.directed: The body and prāṇa themselves are understood as containing or supporting divine powers.

blocks.text: All the subtle processes of embodied manifestation.
blocks.directed: All the subtle processes of embodied manifestation.

blocks.text: And remember the idea that the body can become a support for the entire cosmic path?
blocks.directed: And remember the idea that the body can become a support for the entire cosmic path?

blocks.text: Well, here’s another way in which the body becomes a sacred field.
blocks.directed: Well, here’s another way in which the body becomes a sacred field.

blocks.text: The deities associated with body and prāṇa are ritually nourished through the consecrated substance.
blocks.directed: The deities associated with body and prāṇa are ritually nourished through the consecrated substance.

blocks.text: Because someone might have expected an elaborate instruction about pouring water over the head.
blocks.directed: Because someone might have expected an elaborate instruction about pouring water over the head.

blocks.text: Instead, we’re discussing a mantra-wheel installed in a consecrated vessel and the ritual satisfaction of divine powers embodied within the practitioner.
blocks.directed: Instead, we’re discussing a mantra-wheel installed in a consecrated vessel and the ritual satisfaction of divine powers embodied within the practitioner.

blocks.text: The body is not merely an impure obstacle to divine consciousness. It can be recognised as a field of divine powers.
blocks.directed: The body is not merely an impure obstacle to divine consciousness. It can be recognised as a field of divine powers.

blocks.text: But the ritual requires more than merely possessing the right substances.
blocks.directed: But the ritual requires more than merely possessing the right substances.

blocks.text: What makes it sacred is the process by which those substances, mantras, bodily powers and the worshipper are apprehended through their relationship to Śiva.
blocks.directed: What makes it sacred is the process by which those substances, mantras, bodily powers and the worshipper are apprehended through their relationship to Śiva.

blocks.text: And now, at last, Abhinavagupta returns to the internal bath.
blocks.directed: And now, at last, Abhinavagupta returns to the internal bath.

blocks.text: And this is where the chapter reaches its natural culmination.
blocks.directed: And this is where the chapter reaches its natural culmination.

blocks.text:
8. Internal bathing — you don’t actually need to get wet
Right.
blocks.directed:
8. Internal bathing — you don’t actually need to get wet
Right.

blocks.text: And the Sanskrit is remarkably concise.
blocks.directed: And the Sanskrit is remarkably concise.

blocks.text: Abhinavagupta says that through the contemplative assumption of the forms of earth and the other elements, the practitioner becomes identified with the corresponding circles or groups.
blocks.directed: Abhinavagupta says that through the contemplative assumption of the forms of earth and the other elements, the practitioner becomes identified with the corresponding circles or groups.
[short pause] Now the key word is:

blocks.text: The condition of becoming of that nature.
blocks.directed: The condition of becoming of that nature.

blocks.text: You contemplate the form of earth.
blocks.directed: You contemplate the form of earth.

blocks.text: Not merely as a lump of soil.
blocks.directed: Not merely as a lump of soil.

blocks.text: But as a manifestation of divine power.
blocks.directed: But as a manifestation of divine power.

blocks.text: And through sustained contemplation, you become identified with the relevant divine form.
blocks.directed: And through sustained contemplation, you become identified with the relevant divine form.

blocks.text: Then the remaining forms, according to their appropriate contemplative arrangement.
blocks.directed: Then the remaining forms, according to their appropriate contemplative arrangement.

blocks.text: The process is taking place through consciousness itself.
blocks.directed: The process is taking place through consciousness itself.

blocks.text: You’re not literally transforming the chemical composition of your body into earth, water, fire or sky.
blocks.directed: You’re not literally transforming the chemical composition of your body into earth, water, fire or sky.

blocks.text: You’re cultivating identification with the divine reality expressed through those forms.
blocks.directed: You’re cultivating identification with the divine reality expressed through those forms.

blocks.text: We began the chapter by defining impurity as the conviction that the Self is mixed with something alien to its nature.
blocks.directed: We began the chapter by defining impurity as the conviction that the Self is mixed with something alien to its nature.

blocks.text: And now the internal bath consists of overcoming that separation through contemplative identification.
blocks.directed: And now the internal bath consists of overcoming that separation through contemplative identification.

blocks.text: So the whole chapter is remarkably coherent.
blocks.directed: So the whole chapter is remarkably coherent.

blocks.text: Becoming identified with the divine form.
blocks.directed: Becoming identified with the divine form.

blocks.text: “Abhinava, mate, why bother with all these different forms? Why earth, water, wind and the rest?”
blocks.directed: [short pause] “Abhinava, mate, why bother with all these different forms? Why earth, water, wind and the rest?”

blocks.text: Because different practitioners require different supports.
blocks.directed: Because different practitioners require different supports.

blocks.text: Remember what we established at the beginning?
blocks.directed: Remember what we established at the beginning?

blocks.text: Others require one or several methods.
blocks.directed: Others require one or several methods.

blocks.text: And these methods may operate through the body, external substances, mantras or contemplation.
blocks.directed: And these methods may operate through the body, external substances, mantras or contemplation.

blocks.text: But the important thing is what they accomplish.
blocks.directed: But the important thing is what they accomplish.

blocks.text: They overcome the sense that consciousness is fundamentally separate from the manifestations through which it appears.
blocks.directed: They overcome the sense that consciousness is fundamentally separate from the manifestations through which it appears.

blocks.text: You don’t purify the Self by turning it into Śiva.
blocks.directed: You don’t purify the Self by turning it into Śiva.

blocks.text: It already possesses the nature of Śiva.
blocks.directed: It already possesses the nature of Śiva.

blocks.text: You purify the mistaken identification that obscures that recognition.
blocks.directed: You purify the mistaken identification that obscures that recognition.

blocks.text: And whether the means involves water, fire, mantra, a consecrated substance or contemplative absorption, the decisive point remains:
blocks.directed: [short pause] And whether the means involves water, fire, mantra, a consecrated substance or contemplative absorption, the decisive point remains:

blocks.text: Immersion in the essential nature of the Supreme Lord.
blocks.directed: Immersion in the essential nature of the Supreme Lord.

blocks.text: And it brings us to the actual closing verses.
blocks.directed: And it brings us to the actual closing verses.

blocks.text: 9. The concluding Sanskrit verse — the real bath is immersion in Bhairava
blocks.directed: 9. The concluding Sanskrit verse — the real bath is immersion in Bhairava

blocks.text:
परभैरवसम्मज्जनमाहुः स्नानं यथा तु तद्भवति।तदपि बाह्यं स्नानं न मुख्यमुपचारतः किं तु॥
Parabhairavasammajjanam āhuḥ snānaṃ yathā tu tad bhavati.
blocks.directed:
[slowly] परभैरवसम्मज्जनमाहुः स्नानं यथा तु तद्भवति।तदपि बाह्यं स्नानं न मुख्यमुपचारतः किं तु॥
Parabhairavasammajjanam āhuḥ snānaṃ yathā tu tad bhavati.

blocks.text: Tad api bāhyaṃ snānaṃ na mukhyam upacārataḥ kiṃ tu.
blocks.directed: Tad api bāhyaṃ snānaṃ na mukhyam upacārataḥ kiṃ tu.

blocks.text: This verse is transmitted in the Devanāgarī edition used here, but not in the shorter GRETIL transcription. Its wording contrasts immersion in supreme Bhairava with external bathing, which is not the primary bath. १२ +2
blocks.directed: This verse is transmitted in the Devanāgarī edition used here, but not in the shorter GRETIL transcription. Its wording contrasts immersion in supreme Bhairava with external bathing, which is not the primary bath. १२ +2

blocks.text: And this is what is called bathing.
blocks.directed: And this is what is called bathing.

blocks.text: Figuratively or by conventional ritual designation.
blocks.directed: Figuratively or by conventional ritual designation.

blocks.text: Because Abhinavagupta isn’t saying you shouldn’t wash your body.
blocks.directed: Because Abhinavagupta isn’t saying you shouldn’t wash your body.

blocks.text: He’s saying that washing the body and attaining supreme purity are not identical accomplishments.
blocks.directed: He’s saying that washing the body and attaining supreme purity are not identical accomplishments.

blocks.text: You can put on clean clothes.
blocks.directed: You can put on clean clothes.

blocks.text: But if you’re still completely convinced that your consciousness is fundamentally separate from the universe and the supreme Lord, the metaphysical impurity he’s describing hasn’t been overcome.
blocks.directed: But if you’re still completely convinced that your consciousness is fundamentally separate from the universe and the supreme Lord, the metaphysical impurity he’s describing hasn’t been overcome.

blocks.text: Conversely, the highest purification is not dependent upon the physical cleanliness of the body.
blocks.directed: Conversely, the highest purification is not dependent upon the physical cleanliness of the body.

blocks.text: It’s the recognition of one’s true nature.
blocks.directed: It’s the recognition of one’s true nature.

blocks.text: A Sanskrit textual witness also preserves a further closing stanza in a Middle Indo-Aryan vernacular form, beginning:
blocks.directed: [short pause] A Sanskrit textual witness also preserves a further closing stanza in a Middle Indo-Aryan vernacular form, beginning:

blocks.text: Its message again identifies true bathing with immersion in supreme bliss and the recognition of the highest Self. The stanza is absent from the GRETIL transcription and from the Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism edition, so I’m distinguishing it from the closing Sanskrit verse rather than silently combining the witnesses. १२
blocks.directed: Its message again identifies true bathing with immersion in supreme bliss and the recognition of the highest Self. The stanza is absent from the GRETIL transcription and from the Sanskrit & Trika Shaivism edition, so I’m distinguishing it from the closing Sanskrit verse rather than silently combining the witnesses. १२

blocks.text: And now let’s finish in our own words.
blocks.directed: And now let’s finish in our own words.

blocks.text: You’ve spent your entire life imagining that purity is something you can acquire.
blocks.directed: You’ve spent your entire life imagining that purity is something you can acquire.

blocks.text: Something you can produce through the right action.
blocks.directed: Something you can produce through the right action.

blocks.text: And perhaps you’ve believed that impurity is something genuinely stuck to your essential being.
blocks.directed: And perhaps you’ve believed that impurity is something genuinely stuck to your essential being.

blocks.text: Some condition that separates you from the divine.
blocks.directed: Some condition that separates you from the divine.

blocks.text: What exactly could contaminate unrestricted consciousness?
blocks.directed: What exactly could contaminate unrestricted consciousness?

blocks.text: Even the apparent impurities are manifested through its own freedom.
blocks.directed: Even the apparent impurities are manifested through its own freedom.

blocks.text: The problem isn’t that Śiva has somehow become fundamentally impure.
blocks.directed: The problem isn’t that Śiva has somehow become fundamentally impure.

blocks.text: The problem is that consciousness has taken on an identification that conceals its own nature.
blocks.directed: The problem is that consciousness has taken on an identification that conceals its own nature.

blocks.text: And the moment that identification is overcome?
blocks.directed: And the moment that identification is overcome?

blocks.text: Not because something foreign has been removed from the supreme Self.
blocks.directed: Not because something foreign has been removed from the supreme Self.

blocks.text: But because its nature has become evident.
blocks.directed: But because its nature has become evident.

blocks.text: So you can enter a river.
blocks.directed: So you can enter a river.

blocks.text: You can bathe in sacred water.
blocks.directed: You can bathe in sacred water.

blocks.text: You can engage in internal contemplation.
blocks.directed: You can engage in internal contemplation.

blocks.text: And all these may serve as supports.
blocks.directed: And all these may serve as supports.

blocks.text: The supreme consciousness that is never separate from your own essential being.
blocks.directed: The supreme consciousness that is never separate from your own essential being.

blocks.text: You thought you needed to wash something off yourself to reach Śiva.
blocks.directed: You thought you needed to wash something off yourself to reach Śiva.

blocks.text: Abhinavagupta says the very conviction that you’re something other than Śiva is the impurity.
blocks.directed: Abhinavagupta says the very conviction that you’re something other than Śiva is the impurity.

blocks.text: You don’t wash yourself until you become Śiva. You recognise that even the apparent impurity never possessed an independent reality outside Śiva.
blocks.directed: You don’t wash yourself until you become Śiva. You recognise that even the apparent impurity never possessed an independent reality outside Śiva.

blocks.text: And that recognition is the real purification.
blocks.directed: And that recognition is the real purification.

blocks.text: Choosing a sacred place, installing the Mālinī mantras, transforming the body and ritual implements into Śiva, and performing worship as a living enactment of nonduality.
